newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH "BIG THREE" STOCKS FALL ON PROFIT TAKING.
newsitem.headline: CZECH "BIG THREE" STOCKS FALL ON PROFIT TAKING.

text.p: SPT Telecom, CEZ, and Komercni Banka, the three largest issues on the Prague Stock Exchange, fell in early trading on Wednesday, as investors took profits on the heels of a strong bull run by all three in recent weeks.
SPT shares dropped 119 crowns to 3,866, while CEZ lost 27 crowns to 1,200 and Komercni Banka tumbled 88 crowns to 2,862.
"It's a very thin market and when you see a little profit-taking like we are, the market kind of collapses," said Jan Sykora of Wood and Company.

"SPT is still fundamentally somewhat expensive at these levels and Komercni had a tremendous rise and some are sitting on unrealised profits that they are now taking. I don't expect CEZ to slip much further," he added.
Komercni has gained over 600 crowns in 1997, while CEZ is up more than 100 crowns and SPT over 500 crowns.
The three issues, which comprise almost half of the capitalisation-weighted PX50 index, have been boosted by foreign investors who began taking new positions at the beginning of the year.
